rules.description: BUrlG § 3: at least 24 Werktage (Mon–Sat basis) per year = 20 days on a 5-day week

versions.notes: § 3(1) "Der Urlaub beträgt jährlich mindestens 24 Werktage"; § 3(2) Werktage = all calendar days that are not Sundays or statutory holidays (6-day basis). 20 days on a 5-day week is the pro-rata conversion 24 × 5/6. Verified as the law in force on the verification date; historical effective date not researched, so effectiveFrom is set to 2026-01-01 (earlier dates resolve to the parent/none).

rules.description: EFZG § 3/§ 4: employer continues 100% pay for up to 6 weeks of incapacity; entitlement arises after 4 weeks uninterrupted employment

source.title: Entgeltfortzahlungsgesetz (EFZG) § 3 Anspruch auf Entgeltfortzahlung im Krankheitsfall

versions.notes: § 3(1): continued pay for the period of incapacity up to six weeks; § 3(3): entitlement arises after four weeks of uninterrupted employment; § 4(1) (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/entgfg/__4.html): the pay due for the employee's regular working time is continued (100%). Repeat-illness rules (§ 3(1) sentence 2) and statutory health-insurance Krankengeld after week 6 not modelled. Verified as the law in force on the verification date; historical effective date not researched, so effectiveFrom is set to 2026-01-01 (earlier dates resolve to the parent/none).

rules.description: BGB § 622: 4 weeks to the 15th or month-end; longer employer notice by length of service; 2 weeks during probation (max 6 months)

versions.notes: § 622(1) base; § 622(2) employer notice after 2/5/8/10/12/15/20 years in the business or undertaking: 1/2/3/4/5/6/7 months to the end of a calendar month; § 622(3) agreed probation up to six months: two weeks. Collective-agreement deviations (§ 622(4)) and small-business rules (§ 622(5)) not modelled. Verified as the law in force on the verification date; historical effective date not researched, so effectiveFrom is set to 2026-01-01 (earlier dates resolve to the parent/none).

rules.description: National transposition status of the EU Pay Transparency Directive (EU) 2023/970

source.title: EUR-Lex: national transposition measures communicated for Directive (EU) 2023/970

versions.notes: EUR-Lex lists no national transposition measures for Germany (checked 2026-10-18). The existing Entgelttransparenzgesetz (2017) remains in force but is not a notified transposition. Press/official reports (Bundestag Drs. 21/7026, 8 July 2026 — bundestag.de not on the allow-list) say the ministry draft was still in preparation.
